traits.label: Protests, then obeys
traits.text: Hood repeatedly argues against the order to attack up the Emmetsburg road, proposing an alternative flank attack, but ultimately complies with the command after his protests are rejected.

citation.doc: Hood to Longstreet, June 28, 1875 (Advance and Retreat)
citation.quote: After this urgent protest against entering the battle at Gettysburg, according to instructions—which protest is the first and only one I ever made during my entire military career—I ordered my line to advance and make th

traits.label: Relies on reconnaissance
traits.text: Hood uses the reports from his Texas scouts to assess the enemy's position and the tactical difficulties of the ordered attack before making his decision to protest.

citation.doc: Hood to Longstreet, June 28, 1875 (Advance and Retreat)
citation.quote: I had sent forward some of my picked Texas scouts to ascertain the position of the enemy's extreme left flank.

traits.label: Assesses tactical risk
traits.text: Hood evaluates the terrain and enemy fire, concluding that the ordered attack would result in a 'fearful sacrifice' of his troops, which motivates his request to change the plan.

citation.doc: Hood to Longstreet, June 28, 1875 (Advance and Retreat)
citation.quote: I knew that if the feat was accomplished, it must be at a most fearful sacrifice of as brave and gallant soldiers as ever engaged in battle.
